Component-based architecture for weapons and character features.

description: This work-in-progress project explores the structural and gameplay elements of modern first-person shooters, focusing on immersive player perspective and scalable multiplayer mechanics.
The architecture of the project emphasizes modularity through clearly separated components and ability-driven logic.
The multiplayer logic was designed to support both free-for-all and team scenarios, maintaining a clean separation of game rules, character states, and replicated actions.

elements.description: Enables consistent body awareness in first-person, ensuring alignment between camera, mesh, and animation.
Aiming, firing, and interaction abilities are handled through the ability system to maintain reusability and flexibility.
Built-in support for assigning teams and handling game rules that reflect team alignment.
Movement speed scales dynamically based on attributes, allowing gameplay effects like slow, buffs, and gear to influence mobility via GAS.
Each weapon defines equipped and unequipped weight values that affect the player's speed, adding tactical depth to inventory choices.
Weapons dropped or picked up preserve individual state like magazine count and have synced physics sound feedback when landing.
Reusable actor base supporting health and abilities, used for things like Claymores or Explosive Barrels that respond to damage events.
Optimized texture-based minimap with dynamic, game-driven indicators and a separate layer for team markers or objectives.
Quickly place world markers on screen and minimap to indicate players or locations—supports two active markers per player for tactical communication.

description: This ongoing template serves as a practical space to test GAS logic, multiplayer replication, and camera-animation consistency in first-person games, helping me refine system design under networked conditions.
